packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 12

Only neutral prompt, packet metadata and the supplied two images used. No catalogue, identification or earlier transcription consulted or exposed.

Layout
Two upright photographs of a rectangular leaf, with two broad text columns. Image-001 has a separate short line across the upper margin above the column heads. Its function is uncertain: it is not securely legible as a title. The small brown cursive hand is very faded, especially on image-002, where large areas are almost erased. Broad abrasion/scuffing and discoloration affect both sides. There are no secure colored rubrics, enlarged decorative initials, underlined lemmata or distinct interlinear glosses. A tiny mark at image-001's right margin may be an annotation but is unreadable. No main-text/commentary arrangement can be asserted. The supplied photographs are distinct faces, not overlapping detail crops.

Selection
The top-margin line was inspected first, but cannot be securely read. The left column's middle and final lines of image-001 are clearer than its opening. I chose these for two attempted samples, preserving gaps rather than reconstructing prose. Neither sample amounts to a reliable continuous passage.

Line convention: L = left column of ORIGINAL image, counted from its first visible written baseline. The faded top lines make the ordinal counts approximate. Original y positions identify the lines independently. Abbreviation strokes are approximate; proposed expansions are explicitly parenthesized.

These are tentative letter-group readings only. In particular, existencio?/honestis?/dependet? should not be accepted without checking the pixels. I have not supplied a subject, grammatical continuation or source-based expansion. No definite deletion or addition is visible.

Transforms
Both full images viewed. image-001 is 5000×7065 pixels. Native crops of image-001 inspected at (650,2543)–(2550,3532), (650,4804)–(2550,5793), and (2000,141)–(4900,423). No rotation, filtering, sharpening or restoration. The top-margin crop is wide and was display-scaled; the two prose crops were inspected at native scale. These repeat the same full-image lines.

Unread areas/limitations
All of image-002 and most of image-001 remain untranscribed. The right column was surveyed but did not offer a confidently recoverable opening. Fade and abrasion, rather than a lack of field of view, dominate the problem. Different illumination, multispectral imaging or a specialist second reading is needed to recover checkable connecting prose. This response explicitly does not claim two successfully readable passages.
